sources.citation: Zwisler, Joshua James. 2018. The Pijao of Natagaima: Post-Linguicide Indigenous Identity and Language. Cadernos de Etnolinguistica 6(1): 51-80.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No stress rule. p.55: the only Pijao sources are Simon's short list, Ramirez Sendoya 1952 (mixed-origin dictionary) and 'the Loukokta word list (30 words long)'; 'there is also no record either of the morphosyntax of the Pijao language'. p.70: the remembered-word list from the Natagaima community uses an orthography 'based on, but not identical, to the system used by Durbin and Seijas (1973) with diacritics representing stress' -- acute accents appear on individual items in varying positions (alamán, kienán, tenú final; kahírre, golúpa, toléma penult; çéçira, óreme, túngama initial), most ite…

sources.note: Nothing. pp.2-3: 'Hammarstrom (2015) believes that both Coyaima [coy] and Natagaimas [nts] are simply place names and should be merged into Pijao, citing Durbin and Seijas 1973.' Establishes that Coyaima is not a distinct language.
Nothing; 'This entry has been retired and is featured here only for bookkeeping purposes', merged into [pij] Pijao per CR 2015-042.
